einzeiler: A preview of Blowback's new mini-series on the Israel-U.S. relationship: No Daylight.
kurzfassung: This preview episode introduces Blowback's upcoming three-part mini-series examining the complex and often tense history between the United States and Israel. The series explores key historical friction points, from Harry Truman's initial opposition to a Jewish state to subsequent confrontations under various administrations. Listeners will hear expert interviews and historical analysis detailing how the bilateral relationship evolved into its current state.
stichpunkte: The subscription mini-series No Daylight examines the deep history and friction of the U.S.-Israel relationship across three parts.
The narrative covers the contemporary context of 2026, marked by direct U.S. involvement in the war against Iran alongside Israel.
Episode one focuses on the battle over Israel's foundation and President Harry Truman's initial resistance to a Jewish state.
Subsequent episodes examine Eisenhower's clashes with Israel over the Suez Canal and the 1956 massacre that led to the creation of AIPAC.
The series looks at Nixon and Kissinger formally deputizing Israel as a Cold War proxy in the 1970s.
Ronald Reagan and George H.W. Bush both faced major friction with Israeli leadership over Lebanon, spy operations, and West Bank settlements.
George H.W. Bush notably withheld ten billion dollars in loan guarantees during a high-stakes standoff with Israeli leadership.
Interviews with scholars like Rashid Khalidi, Douglas Rossenau, and Seth Anziska form the research backbone of the project.

clips.text: Following disrespectful treatment by a newly elected Israeli leader, Bill Clinton expressed private frustration about the power dynamic between the two nations.

clips.hook: Ten billion dollars in loan guarantees withheld
clips.text: President George H.W. Bush engaged in an unprecedented standoff with Israel by freezing massive loan guarantees to demand a halt to West Bank settlements.

clips.hook: Jews made up roughly one-third of the population
clips.text: By the end of World War II, the Jewish minority constituted about a third of mandatory Palestine while leadership aimed to establish complete control over the entire territory.

clips.hook: Truman's private remarks on New York's demographics
clips.text: In a letter to his cousin after visiting New York City, Harry Truman made derogatory demographic observations reflecting the casual prejudice of his era.

clips.hook: Nobody seemed to think I was aware of anything
clips.text: Reflecting years later on official State Department memos, Harry Truman recalled how bureaucrats patronizingly warned him to leave Middle Eastern affairs to the experts.
